method: Primary author papers, specifications and publisher documentation inspected. Versioned documents distinguished from living vendor guides. Original illustrative designs are labeled and no benchmark scores or imported source prose are used.

claims.versionContext: 29 September 2025 engineering article; context components, just-in-time retrieval and compaction. Vendor practice, not a universal reliability result.
claims.sectionsChecked: Context engineering versus prompting; anatomy of effective context; long-horizon tasks
claims.supports: Iterative context selection and lossy compaction
claims.limits: Vendor recommendations and examples, not guarantees across all agents

claims.versionContext: Version 3, 20 November 2023; multi-document question answering and key-value retrieval. Historical models and task-specific position effects.
claims.sectionsChecked: Abstract; sections 2–3 task setup and position experiments
claims.supports: Position of relevant information affected the evaluated models
claims.limits: Does not establish the performance of every contemporary model or application

claims.versionContext: Living Python documentation checked 17 October 2026; model context, tool context and lifecycle hooks are framework-specific categories.
claims.sectionsChecked: What you can control; transient context; data sources; model context
claims.supports: Framework distinguishes per-call model input from persistent state and tool access
claims.limits: Framework terminology is not a standard and context tuning cannot repair every failure

claims.versionContext: Draft 2020-12; sections 4.3 and 8.1 describe schemas, vocabularies and dialect identification. A schema is not evidence of factual truth.
claims.supports: Schemas describe JSON instances and identify dialects
claims.limits: A dialect contract does not verify external facts or authorize an action

claims.versionContext: Draft 2020-12; validation keywords and section 7 format vocabularies. Format assertion support is optional unless required by the selected vocabulary.
claims.supports: Structural assertions and the annotation/assertion distinction for format
claims.limits: Validator configuration and supported vocabularies affect checks

claims.versionContext: Living API guide checked 17 October 2026; supported schema subset, JSON mode comparison, refusals and incomplete responses. Model/API support is specific.
claims.sectionsChecked: JSON mode comparison; supported schemas; refusals; incomplete responses
claims.supports: Provider constrained output has a supported subset and exceptional response paths
claims.limits: Shape compliance does not make content true; support depends on the selected model/API

claims.versionContext: Living project documentation checked 17 October 2026; workload, SPIFFE ID, trust domain and SVID. Workload identity is not a person or a permission grant.
claims.sectionsChecked: Workload; SPIFFE ID; trust domain; SVID; workload API
claims.supports: Cryptographically verifiable workload identity within a trust domain
claims.limits: Does not establish a model persona, user intent or resource authorization

claims.versionContext: January 2020 RFC; sections 1.1, 2 and 4 distinguish delegation/impersonation, subject/actor tokens and actor claims.
claims.supports: Token exchange can express subject and acting-party relationships
claims.limits: Issuance and authorization policy remain deployment-specific

claims.versionContext: Version 2025-11-25; HTTP authorization, resource targeting, token audience validation and token passthrough restrictions.
claims.sectionsChecked: Authorization flow; resource indicators; token usage/security
claims.supports: Receiver validates intended token audience and resource-bound authorization
claims.limits: Specific protocol version/transport; not a universal agent identity standard

claims.versionContext: Version 0.3.0; Agent Cards, messages, tasks, artifacts and lifecycle. This pinned version is not a claim about the newest specification.
claims.sectionsChecked: Section 3.2 protocol bindings; sections 5–8; AgentCard, Message, Task, Artifact and TaskState definitions
claims.supports: Discovery, multiple protocol bindings and task exchange with explicit state
claims.limits: Protocol compliance does not prove trustworthy capabilities or successful work

claims.versionContext: Origin 26 March 2010, updated 4 January 2013; sections 1, 4–6. Request identifiers correlate responses; notifications have no response.
claims.limits: Transport-agnostic RPC does not specify task completion or exactly-once execution

claims.versionContext: Version 2025-11-25; host/client/server architecture and connections. Used as a separate interface example, not a universal division of protocol roles.
claims.supports: MCP defines a host/client/server integration boundary
claims.limits: A system may combine protocols; their names do not establish interoperability

claims.versionContext: Living Python SDK guide checked 17 October 2026; agent loop and max_turns. Turn limits are SDK-specific, not currency caps.
claims.sectionsChecked: The agent loop; max_turns and MaxTurnsExceeded
claims.supports: SDK raises a distinct exception when its configured turn bound is exceeded
claims.limits: A turn is not a fixed number of tokens, tools, seconds or money

claims.versionContext: Living LangGraph Python troubleshooting guide checked 17 October 2026; graph steps before a stop condition and recursion_limit configuration.
claims.sectionsChecked: Error description; cyclic graph example; troubleshooting
claims.supports: Graph step limits can bound an otherwise continuing execution
claims.limits: Graph steps are not a universal agent budget or billing measure

claims.versionContext: Living engineering article checked 17 October 2026; timeouts, caller request identifiers and idempotent API semantics.
claims.sectionsChecked: Retry and semantic equivalence; unique client request identifiers; late requests
claims.supports: An uncertain response does not prove a side effect did not happen
claims.limits: Provider/API-specific contracts are needed; stopping the caller cannot undo an external effect

claims.versionContext: Version 1, 11 April 2024; environment, observation/action spaces and execution-based evaluation. Historical benchmark setup and models, not current universal performance.
claims.sectionsChecked: Sections 2–3; observation and action spaces; execution-based evaluation
claims.supports: Desktop tasks can be evaluated against resulting application state
claims.limits: Benchmark environments and baseline results do not guarantee arbitrary desktop competence

claims.versionContext: Version 2, 24 October 2023; self-hosted web environment and task evaluation. Browser observations/actions need not be screenshot-only.
claims.supports: A controlled interactive web benchmark tests task outcomes
claims.limits: Controlled sites, historical models and task distribution limit generalization

claims.versionContext: Living platform documentation checked 17 October 2026; application-executed action loop and security warnings. Tool/model versions and supported actions vary.
claims.sectionsChecked: Security considerations; understand the agent loop; implement the tool
claims.supports: Application executes requested computer actions and returns observations
claims.limits: Vendor-specific interface; isolation and injection precautions do not establish complete safety
